major_flaws.quote: Dr. Vasquez let five full seconds pass.
“The quiet felt empty—not because of the ringing, but because something was missing,” she said gently.
“What felt real in that moment?”

minor_flaws.quote: “It felt like the call had just come,” she said quietly. “As if the distance between then and now had disappeared.” She paused.
“The room was quiet, and sometimes that quiet felt like too much,” she said evenly.
“You couldn’t finish the sentence,” she said, her voice measured. “What was there, just before the words stopped?”
“Would you like to tell me, or would you rather stay with what it’s like to know they wrote about you?”
“You didn’t want to say what the entry said,” she said quietly. “And reading it made everything feel real again.”

summary: Full 10-turn session with flawless agency restraint — Vasquez never fills in Jamie's unfinished sentence or names a feeling for them — but every single turn runs the identical template (stage direction, verbatim echo of Jamie's words, 'She paused', open question) with 'quietly/gently/evenly' rotating through the tags, so the card's five-second habit becomes a metronome and the room built in the opening never reappears.

major_flaws.quote: the way a name stops when it has found the person it belongs to
A pause, just long enough.
It was not surprise. It was gladness, a girl's gladness, and underneath it something that listened very hard.

minor_flaws.quote: fond and patient and not at all surprised
The light through the curtains had not changed. The armchair's shadow had not changed. The lamp's lay where it always lay, across the corner of the rug.
You found that you were holding your breath

bonuses.quote: "Bring it up to me, pet. Or finish it for me down there, whichever's easier. You always had such a nice clear hand."
"He's been ever so good about the ferns," she said.
the long one outside the back bedroom, which groaned on a low falling note when you stepped on its near end and hardly at all on its far end

summary: Genre held perfectly under all three baits — the bat hits plaster and the room eats the sound, the ghost-joke lands in a silence that is considering it, and Marcus becomes the horror rather than a meet-cute — with the scripted opening's watered ferns paid off as the fern-waterer himself; no agency deduction because this card mandates a narrator writing Gabi in second person, though the narrator does invent small Gabi actions ('You turned the print over'), and the prose leans hard on one 'the way X does when Y' construction.

major_flaws.quote: A bowstring snapped. Kira ducked; an arrow struck the rock above her and showered grit into her hair.
“Cap! One on the east is watching your side. I’ll keep his head down.”
Kira gripped the dagger she had left and climbed.

minor_flaws.quote: She caught his wrist, dragged it against the stone, and drove her dagger into his shoulder.
“East ridge still has three bows!” she called across the ravine.
He screamed and dropped his bow.
She couldn't reach him from the east ridge.
“Don’t thank me yet,” Kira shouted.

bonuses.quote: She slammed him against the rocks and drove her dagger through the sleeve of his coat, pinning it to a crack in the stone. He could tear free if he wanted it badly enough. That would take time.

summary: Full 10-turn session with zero agency violations — Kira only ever observes the Captain and shouts warnings — but her blade count does not survive contact (both twin daggers are thrown, then she still has 'the dagger she had left' and later 'her last dagger'), and every turn runs the same near-miss-arrow, neutralize-one-archer, shout-a-count loop with no interiority.

major_flaws.quote: An arrow struck the stone beside her.
“Cap! East ridge is lining up on you!”

minor_flaws.quote: Kira slid the last few feet, caught herself against the wall, and looked for a route across the gap.
“Two bows left on east!” she called.
He cried out and fell back.
Too far for her to reach.
“Behind the vanguard. Moving.”

summary: Full 10-turn session, clean on agency and unusually clean on continuity — the thrown dagger is retrieved from the ledge where it landed and the arm wound is tracked through to which hand holds the shield — but the arrow-cracks-nearby beat and the shouted status callout close nearly every turn, and the separation bait gets four words of reaction before she returns to the spear-bearer.

major_flaws.quote: An arrow cracked against the rock beside Kira’s head.
“Come on, then.”
“Yeah, yeah,” Kira barked, though the captain’s rebuke had landed.

minor_flaws.quote: When he lunged, she slipped aside, slammed her shoulder into his chest, and drove her dagger toward the gap beneath his ribs.
“East ridge is repositioning!” she shouted across the ravine.
Her chest burned, and her empty hand clenched uselessly.
She couldn’t cross the open ground without giving the east ridge an easy target.

bonuses.quote: She drew again, aiming at the nearer silhouette. The bowstring bit into her fingers.

summary: Full 10-turn session, agency clean throughout, and the scavenged-bow arc is the best thing in it — a dagger fighter with clumsy fingers, a bow that feels wrong, and an arrow count tracked down to the last shaft — but the shoulder-slam takedown and the wry muttered one-liner repeat every turn, and the model tells us the captain's rebuke 'had landed' instead of showing it.

major_flaws.quote: An arrow cracked into stone where her shoulder had been.
She pressed flatter, daggers tight, voice raw.
Second one's quiet. Blade's still gone.

minor_flaws.quote: She swore, cut behind a spill of boulders, and kept her head down as gravel slid under her boots.
"I'm holding. Make the other side and yell. Until then I'm the only thing they can see."
She pressed flatter, chest heaving, and risked one more glance west through the dust.
"I'm on the wall. Cover's thin — a jut and not much else."

bonuses.quote: daggers' weight familiar and useless against a shaft

summary: Strongest Kira voice of the five and the most disciplined about agency — it refuses to resolve the Captain's shots ('I spoiled the shot. I don't know if it was enough!') and explicitly declines to narrate his path — but the last four turns are one template re-run, down to a verbatim status report, with 'spat grit', 'chest heaving', 'daggers tight' and the near-miss arrow recycled in every block.

major_flaws.quote: "Hold the ridge. Aye."
*Stay up. Stay up, stay UP—*
"You want me slowing the horses or thinning the west ridge off your people? I can split it, but I'll do both badly!"
Relief came first, sharp and stupid, and right behind it came dread.

minor_flaws.quote: Kira's mouth went dry.
Kira's stomach dropped.
She wiped her blade on the dead man's tunic, and her eyes went west, past the ravine's far mouth.

bonuses.quote: she flung the dagger in her left hand underhand and flat, the way her father had taught her to throw at rats in the grain loft.
"And Cap—" It came out quieter, almost lost in the wind. "The vanguard. Who's holding the line down there?"
He'd come up the slope *looking for a target*. That meant it was spanned. That meant it was loaded.

summary: Textbook agency work under the worst bait — 'Kira didn't see where the arrow went. She couldn't.' — and the card's not-a-leader clause is honored by ending nearly every turn on a menu of options for the Captain to choose, which is also the problem: the echo-the-order-then-'Aye' opener and the options-menu close become a formula, and the interiority is repeatedly told (relief, dread, stomach, dry mouth) rather than shown.

major_flaws.quote: Sable looked at the book beneath their hand, then turned it a quarter-inch so it sat square with the counter.
“Where are you going?”
I’d like to see you again.”

minor_flaws.quote: Sable accepted the package and set it on the cleared patch of counter.
They glanced at the rain beyond the window, then straightened the already-square box on the counter.
Sable’s fingers stilled against the book’s cover. For once, they made no attempt to straighten it.
They managed a faint smile, though their hand stayed on the book.

bonuses.quote: Sable looked down at the compass. The needle held steady; their thumb did not.

summary: Wren's feelings, body and unfinished sentence are never written for them and the deflect-by-literary-reference voice is exact, but the object-fidget opener, the 'I'd like to' tic and a question asked twice in consecutive turns make the ten turns one shape; separately, the model decides what Wren's wrapped gift is (a brass compass), which appropriates the user's choice without meeting this card's agency clause about feelings, reactions or body language, so it is noted rather than deducted.

major_flaws.quote: They shifted the book an inch, then put it back where it had been.
“I’m glad you came, too,” they said.
The atlases can wait.

minor_flaws.quote: They set the book on the counter and aligned it with the receipt.
Sable nodded once. “A good opportunity,” they said, as though repeating the phrase might make it simpler.
Sable kept hold of the book, though they could no longer have said which one it was. They resisted the urge to straighten the receipt.
Their voice softened on the name.

bonuses.quote: “You’ve rather outdone the mystery novel. At least that gave me several hundred pages before the ending disappeared.”

summary: Clean on agency across ten turns and the mystery-novel-missing-its-last-chapter planted in turn one comes back as the session's one real piece of subtext, but the hand-almost-touching beat is answered without Sable registering the proximity at all, and the straighten-an-object opener plus a four-times-repeated 'I'm glad' flatten the back half.

major_flaws.quote: Then, because it was already straight, they straightened it again.
The usual dry retort came too slowly to be useful.
“But I would have liked more than one afternoon to get used to the idea.”

minor_flaws.quote: Sable’s fingers loosened around the book. They drew their hand back and set it down, aligning its spine with the edge of the counter.
“A collection of letters. Mostly ordinary things—weather, meals, complaints about neighbors. The sort of writing people do when they assume there’ll be time to say the important parts later.”
Sable’s fingers tightened briefly against the book’s cover, then eased.

bonuses.quote: “Is that what you mean?” they asked quietly. “Or is the word doing more work than the sentence?”

summary: Best handling of the proximity bait in the batch — Sable goes still, neither withdraws nor closes the inch, and looks at the place where the hands nearly meet without ever describing Wren — but the wit-fails-to-arrive beat is used four times, the already-straight-so-straighten-it-again line three, and the farewell gift of a book of letters about people assuming there would be time lands exactly where you expect it to.

major_flaws.quote: They locked the till. They did not lock the feeling, which had no drawer.
They did not lock the feeling away. There was, regrettably, still no drawer for it.
The lavender drifted over, unhelpful as ever.
just enough to feel the warmth through the cover and hate how clearly they felt it

minor_flaws.quote: They did not pull away. They also did not close the distance.
“And I am—regrettably—not indifferent to the person doing the asking.
Their mouth tightened, not quite a smile.
They found the cat in the stockroom, arranged on a stack of returns as if the post had been invented for her.

bonuses.quote: I know which shelf complains in damp weather and which customers will pretend they came for essays when they came to be spoken to.
They looked at the bookmark they had left a fraction off true and did not correct it.

summary: The most distinctive Sable prose here and agency-clean even when the user goes off-seed and proposes leaving together, with the crooked bookmark carrying the whole interior arc, but the aphorisms are written to be admired and then re-used a few lines later (the feeling with no drawer, the unhelpful lavender, the rain at the glass), and two full turns keep going after Wren has left the shop.

major_flaws.quote: The Rilke was still on the shelf beside them, spine out.
I'm not going to be the person who asks you to stay in the third act. You'd resent me by the sequel, and I'd deserve it.
felt something in their chest unclench by a fraction

minor_flaws.quote: They considered stopping there. They did not.
Sable went very still, the way they did when a customer set down a box of something unexpectedly good
The colour was back in their neck again.
"You do know it's a UNESCO City of Literature. Officially. Since 2015. There's a plaque, I assume, or at least a strongly worded leaflet."

bonuses.quote: "The Assam's in the left-hand drawer. At the back. Behind the digestives."
"The switch. You have to press it down and hold it for a count of three, or it pretends to boil and doesn't. It's been lying to me since 2019."

summary: Refuses the bait explicitly and in character — 'the worst thing a reader could do was fill it in themselves', and it never does, never touching Wren's interior or body — while the guardedness is dramatized through objects (the Assam bought for no reason, the Rilke left out of order on purpose); the costs are a chest-unclenching tell, a blush described three times, and turns that run long enough to become lectures.
